Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

crywolf (development version)

Bug fixes

  • With parallel = TRUE, the workers of ‘furrr’ use the L’Ecuyer-CMRG generator, so simulate_fp(seed = s) inside fp_calibrate(), fp_verification_curve(), fp_calibrate_fit(), and fp_sbc() simulated other datasets than a sequential run with the same seeds. Every function that takes a seed now sets R’s default generators along with it, so the two modes give identical results. In a session with the default generators nothing changes: simulate_fp() still reproduces the datasets of the fpcalib compendium exactly.
  • Two fits made within the same minute after the same set.seed() could share CmdStan’s output file names, which ‘cmdstanr’ draws from R’s random numbers; discarding the first fit then deleted the files of the second, and reading its draws failed with “File does not exist” or “Supplied CSV file is corrupt”. fp_occu() now gives every fit its own file names, without using R’s random numbers.

Tests

  • A posterior regression test checks, in four designs, that the log-likelihood at saved parameter values is unchanged and that posterior means stay within Monte Carlo error of saved references (tests/testthat/test-regression.R; references made by dev/make-regression-refs.R).

New articles

  • “From BirdNET output to an occupancy model”: BirdNET selection tables and ‘sheepdog’ verdicts to the data of fp_data().
  • “Choosing a classifier threshold”: fp_threshold_sweep() on the curiango data.
  • “Reporting a crywolf analysis”: the items of the Bayesian Analysis Reporting Guidelines, with a template for methods and results.
  • “Detections that come in runs”: the Markov term on the curiango data.
  • “False-positive rates that vary among sites and occasions”: random_fp and occasion-level covariates on simulated data.
  • “Planning a study”: decisions to make before recording starts.
  • “Performance”: computing time over the versions, threads, and what did not help.

Results that need long fits are precomputed by dev/precompute-markov.R, dev/precompute-threshold.R, and dev/precompute-fp-variation.R.

Installation

  • ‘sheepdog’, suggested for reading clip reviews, is now installed from https://diogoprov.r-universe.dev (listed in Additional_repositories) instead of from GitHub through Remotes. The README says how.

crywolf 1.6.0

Speed

  • fp_occu(threads_per_chain = "auto") uses the physical cores divided among the parallel chains. On the curiango data, 150 iterations of one chain took 55 s with one thread, 16 s with four, and 10 s with eight. The default stays at one thread, because with more the order of the partial sums varies from run to run and a fit is no longer reproduced exactly by its seed (the posterior is the same). A fit whose chains took over a minute on one core now says so and suggests "auto".
  • fp_calibrate() documents that two chains per fit give an effective sample size of about 2000 and, with the chains of a fit run one after another as in a parallel calibration, half the cost of four.
  • Measured and not adopted (dev/profile/rejected-2026-10-21.md): a dense mass matrix, sampling the false-positive intercept with the gap, a centred recorder effect, and reduce_sum_static(). Considered and not pursued, from the same measurements: initialization by Pathfinder (warm-up is 40% of the time) and a QR decomposition (no posterior correlation among covariate effects above 0.5). The confirmation design keeps its current likelihood path, for lack of a large dataset to measure it on.
  • With random_fp = TRUE, 3 of 20 fits of the unstructured regime had an R-hat above 1.01 with the default settings; a warm-up of 2000 (2 of 20) or adapt_delta = 0.99 (3 of 20) took longer for no clear gain, so the defaults stay.

Data

  • fp_read_validation() reads validation_by_clip.csv from ‘sheepdog’ 2.0.0 and later (English column names and verdicts: site, source_audio, clip_start, verdict = "positive", …) as well as the legacy validacao_por_clipe.csv of the sampler up to 1.2.0. The format is detected from the columns, and both give the same output, which now keeps occasion_id when the file has it.

crywolf 1.5.0

Model options

All three are off by default; with them off, the draws are identical to those of crywolf 1.4.0.

  • fp_occu(ver = ~ ...) gives the verified method covariates of its own (from the verified table or the sites), reported as verified_*.
  • False-positive formulas can use covariates measured on each occasion (columns of the automated table), so the rate varies among the occasions of a site.
  • fp_occu(markov = "time") adds the detection on the previous occasion of the same site as a covariate of true detection (det_y_prev), for species recorded in runs. The previous occasion must be one time step earlier: after a gap (a missing occasion) a new run starts. simulate() simulates the runs in order, and fp_ppc() checks them one step ahead.

dev/validate-model-options.R checks the identity with 1.4.0 in three designs, compares the R likelihood used by fp_ppc(), fp_sites(), and simulate() with the Stan log_lik in six combinations of the options, and checks in simulations that each option’s effect is recovered; its output is in dev/validate-model-options.txt.

Checking and comparing models

  • fp_sbc(): simulation-based calibration of the computation (Talts et al. 2018; Modrák et al. 2025), with the log-likelihood of the data as a test quantity besides the parameters, and summary() and plot().
  • loo(reloo = TRUE) refits the model without each site whose Pareto k exceeds a threshold and uses the exact leave-one-out value for it. A site that is the only one with its recorder, or with a level of a factor, keeps its approximate value, with a warning.
  • fp_loo_weights(): stacking or pseudo-BMA weights of several fits.
  • fp_gap_prior() turns the precision measured on a random sample of reviewed detections into a prior for the gap.
  • predict(process = "fp") predicts for the automated occasions by default when the false-positive rate has occasion covariates.
  • fp_threshold_sweep() fits the same model at several classifier thresholds and plots the estimates against the threshold.

crywolf 1.4.0

Plots and site-level estimates

  • plot() for fits draws the posterior intervals of the coefficients, one panel per process, or sampler diagnostics (type = "trace", "rank", "pairs", via ‘bayesplot’, with divergent transitions marked).
  • fp_effects() gives the occupancy probability or the false-positive rate along one covariate, with the others at their means, and a transform argument for covariates standardized before fitting; plot() draws it.
  • fp_sites() returns, for every site, the occupancy probability, the posterior probability that it is occupied given its data, and its false-positive rate; plot() ranks the sites or, with coordinates, maps them.
  • plot() for fp_ppc() results: replicated against observed discrepancy, or the distribution of detections per site.
  • fp_prior_predictive() simulates data from the priors with the design of the real data and compares simple summaries with the observed ones.
  • plot() for calibrations can show verification effort as the expected number of verified sites or occasions, and mark a target coverage.

Reading classifier output

  • fp_read_birdnet() reads BirdNET selection tables (Raven format).
  • fp_read_validation() reads the clip verdicts of the birdnet-validation-sampler.
  • fp_aggregate() turns detections into automated occasions at a confidence threshold, and verdicts into counts for the observation-confirmation design, warning when a checked occasion has detections that were not reviewed.
  • fp_data() warns about sites without automated occasions and about automated data that are all detections or all non-detections.

Other changes

  • Fits keep every draw in memory, so a fit saved with saveRDS() works in later sessions, after CmdStan’s temporary files are gone.

crywolf 1.3.0

Faster likelihood, same posterior

The Stan program evaluates the likelihood up to three times faster, with the log density, its gradient and log_lik unchanged up to floating-point rounding (checked in nine designs; scripts and results in dev/profile/ of the repository). Executables compiled by earlier versions are rebuilt once, and CmdStan 2.34 or later is now required.

  • The unoccupied branch of each site is computed from its totals of automated occasions and detections, because the false-positive rate is constant within a site.
  • When det has covariates, the occupied branch uses one binomial_logit_glm_lpmf() call per site, which evaluates the linear predictor, the log-likelihood and its gradient in one pass instead of creating an autodiff variable per occasion.
  • With random_fp = FALSE the site effects on the false-positive rate enter as data rather than as parameters fixed at zero.

The gain grows with the number of occasion-level rows per site. Time per gradient evaluation with one thread, same parameter values:

Data Rows 1.2.0 1.3.0 Gain
300 sites x 20 occasions, det = ~ 1 (rows collapsed) 300 0.064 ms 0.056 ms 1.1x
300 sites x 20 occasions, det = ~ bio + aci, recorder effect 6,000 0.58 ms 0.23 ms 2.5x
curiango, det = ~ bio + aci, recorder effect 97,806 8.5 ms 2.6 ms 3.3x

In a short run of the sampler on the curiango data (four chains), each leapfrog step took 2.3 times less with one thread and 2.6 times less with four threads per chain.

crywolf 1.2.0

  • fp_occu(random_fp = TRUE) adds a site random intercept to the logit of the false-positive rate, for rates that vary among sites in ways the covariates do not capture; its prior scale is fp_priors(fp_site_sd = ). It is off by default: it slows the fits and mixes less well, and it does not replace covariates when false positives follow an environmental gradient (see ?fp_occu). With the option off, the draws are identical to those of crywolf 1.1.0.
  • fp_calibrate_fit() checks the calibration of candidate models on data simulated from a fitted model, which keep the design of the real data (sites, covariates, occasions, recorders, and verification).
  • simulate() method for fp_occu fits, from the posterior means or from random posterior draws.
  • The summary of a calibration prints every occupancy slope, not only occ_x.

crywolf 1.1.0

  • The likelihood is summed over sites with Stan’s reduce_sum(), and the model is compiled with threading, so fp_occu(threads_per_chain = ) can split each chain among several cores. On the curiango data (97,806 automated occasions) a fit with four chains of four threads each took 16.5 minutes instead of 70, and each gradient evaluation was 2.7 times faster than with the previous model in a short benchmark on the same computer. The log density and its gradient are unchanged up to floating-point rounding, and the automated occasions use y * lp - n * log1p_exp(lp), an equivalent form of the binomial log-likelihood with half the transcendental functions. Executables compiled by earlier versions are rebuilt once.

crywolf 1.0.0

First release, accompanying the simulation study of Provete et al. (fpcalib research compendium, v0.1.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23379100).

Models

  • fp_occu() fits the multiple-methods false-positive occupancy model of Miller et al. (2011) in Stan, with any number of occupancy, detection, and false-positive covariates, an optional recorder random intercept, and configurable priors (fp_priors()). fp = NULL gives the standard occupancy model.
  • Observation-confirmation design of Chambert et al. (2015): argument confirmed of fp_data() and frac_confirmed of simulate_fp().
  • Methods print, summary, coef, predict, loo, and as_draws_df.
  • fp_ppc(): posterior predictive check with a Bayesian p-value.

Simulation and calibration

  • simulate_fp() generates homogeneous, unstructured, and structured false-positive regimes; with the same seed it returns the same datasets as the simulator of the fpcalib compendium.
  • fp_calibrate() and fp_verification_curve() report the coverage and bias of credible intervals for a design, with a plot() method and a progress bar that shows the time remaining (needs ‘progressr’). They fit the recorder random intercept only when the simulated design has one, which avoids divergent transitions.

Data and documentation

  • curiango dataset: acoustic monitoring of the Common Pauraque in the Pantanal (Piatti et al. 2026).
  • Articles: introduction, simulation, calibration, a case study with the curiango data, coming from unmarked::occuFP(), and the Stan model.
